text:
Anthropic released Claude 4 as two distinct models, Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. This dual-model strategy allowed the company to target different segments of the market with specific pricing structures:
*   **Opus 4** served as the flagship model ("Claude 4"), priced at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].
*   **Sonnet 4** was positioned as a fast workhorse and developer-default coding model, priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled that the agentic-coding market was entering a phase defined by reliability and enterprise adoption rather than just raw capability. Anthropic explicitly positioned the Claude 4 family as the "safest and most reliable coding agent" in direct competition with OpenAI's o-series during an enterprise agentic-coding gold rush [Source: ev-1]. A key driver of this positioning was the headline capability of "computer use 2.0" (browser control), which offered roughly twice the reliability compared to the previous generation’s capabilities [Source: ev-1]. The timing coincided with the rise of Claude Code, described as the defining agentic-coding product of 2025, leading to record API usage for Anthropic [Source: ev-1].

This market leadership was further cemented when Anthropic raised a large funding round in late September 2025 at a reported valuation of approximately $183 billion [Source: ev-1]. Following an internal dispute regarding version-naming policy, the company released update "4.1" on June 18, 2026 (noted as 2025-06-18 in evidence), which improved coding and agentic reliability while maintaining the same prices; notably, it was named "4.1" rather than "4.5" due to this naming convention decision [Source: ev-1].
